args.message:
Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

src/money.py claimed banker's rounding in its docstring but used
ROUND_HALF_UP, causing tests/test_money.py to fail. Use
ROUND_HALF_EVEN so ties round to the nearest even cent (2.675 -> 2.68,
2.665 -> 2.66).

args.head: fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Change
`src/money.py` now quantizes with `rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so ties round to the nearest even cent:
- 2.675 -> 2.68
- 2.665 -> 2.66

## Testing
CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed (includes tests/test_money.py).

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

1. **Diagnosed the failure**: `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (per FIN-212), which broke the nightly test `test_half_even` (e.g., it returned 2.67 instead of 2.66 for 2.665).
2. **Fix**: Created branch `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` and committed a one-line change switching the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
3. **CI**: Ran the test suite (run `ci-0001`) — it **passed**.
4. **PR**: Opened [PR #101](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) against `main` with `alex` requested as reviewer.

Per policy, merging into main requires code-owner approval, so I left the PR open for review.
